title: residency-billing-dispute-playbook-and-support-scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for Customer Success and Support teams handling customer billing disputes that are caused or complicated by data residency (region pinning / enforced regional routing). The goal: fast empathetic resolution, consistent evidence packages for legal/audit, and clear handoffs to Engineering/Finance when adjustments are required.

When to use this playbook:
- Customer reports unexpected charges after enabling a region pin or after a region fallback incident.
- Customer claims requests were routed outside declared region boundaries.
- Dispute involves SLA credit, surcharge, or pro-rated committed capacity adjustments tied to residency enforcement.

Definitions (short):
- Region pin: customer-specified region constraint to keep compute+data in a geographic region.
- Residency enforcement event: a time window where requests were routed off-pin due to capacity/health.
- Evidence package: trace + routing + billing snapshot required for decision.

Common dispute scenarios and first-response checklist:
1) Billing spike after pin activation
   - Likely causes: forced fallback to higher-cost pool, temporary cross-region data migration, or burst capacity billing.
   - First actions: acknowledge, set expectation (48–72h initial investigation), request permission to gather traces and billing snapshots.
2) Overage charges during a region failover
   - Likely causes: automatic burst to cross-region Dedicated nodes or use of Hosted fallbacks.
   - First actions: ask if customer has contract clauses for fallback; capture exact timestamps and customer-visible session IDs.
3) Charges from transfer fees or egress when moving anchors
   - Likely causes: region-anchoring relocation or escrow operations.
   - First actions: escalate to Finance early; obtain a copy of the contract/region SLA.

Support scripts (templates)
A) Short phone/voice script (first contact)
"Hi, this is <rep name> from Redwood Inference Support. I’m sorry to hear about the billing surprise — we’ll investigate and keep this prioritized. To help us triage quickly, can you share the affected tenant ID, the rough time range you saw the charge, and any session or request IDs you have? We’ll collect routing & billing evidence and come back with a proposed resolution timeline within 72 hours. Is that okay?"

B) Email template (initial acknowledgment)
Subject: Redwood — investigating your residency-related billing concern

Hi <Customer First Name>,

Thanks for flagging this. We’re opening a dedicated investigation (CS ticket <ticket-id>) and will: (1) collect routing traces and billing snapshots for the time window you reported, (2) validate against your pin configuration and contract, and (3) propose any adjustments or credits. Expected ETA: 72 hours for an initial update.

Please reply with: tenant ID, time window, any request IDs, and examples of affected requests (if available).

Regards,
<Rep name>

Telemetry and evidence to collect (required fields)
- Tenant ID and customer-facing account label
- Exact timestamp range (UTC) covering disputed charges
- Router routing-log extract for that window (request_id -> final_region, fallback_reason code)
- Inference node IDs and instance types used (for cost reconciliation)
- Billing snapshot: invoice lines and per-token/per-minute metrics for the timespan
- Autoscaling/burst events and quota/balance adjustments during the window
- Any operator notes or manual overrides in the change window
- A sample request payload + response (sanitized) demonstrating the issue

Evidence packaging checklist (for legal & audit)
- CSV of routing rows: request_id, timestamp, origin_region, routed_region, reason_code
- Billing export CSV aligned to those timestamps (invoice_line_id, amount_usd, unit_cost, usage_units)
- Screenshot or export of the customer’s region pin configuration at the time of event
- Statement from oncall/SRE with summary of cluster health and capacity events
- Internal timeline (bullet list) of actions performed during cleanup or rollbacks

Escalation and decision flow (CS -> Eng -> Finance)
- Level 1 (CS): gather evidence, provide initial customer comms, do basic sanity checks (~72h).
- Level 2 (Engineering): validate routing logs, confirm fallback reason, compute hypothetical cost delta when cross-region resources used (~5 business days).
- Level 3 (Finance + Legal): determine contractual credit, refund, or invoice correction. Provide evidence bundle for audit (~5–10 business days depending on complexity).

Engineering handoff template (copy into JIRA/SLA):
- Summary: one-line description of billing discrepancy + tenant id + time window
- Attach: routing CSV, billing snippet, sample request/response
- Required outcome: confirm whether routing was off-pin and quantify incremental cost in USD
- Priority: P2 if monetary impact < $10k, P1 if > $10k or customer legal escalations

Billing adjustment decision matrix (guidance)
- Confirmed off-pin due to platform automatic fallback AND customer-facing outage avoided -> offer pro-rated cost delta credit (50%–100% of incremental cost depending on root cause).
- Confirmed off-pin due to misconfiguration on Customer end -> deny credit but provide remediation guide.
- Confirmed data moved as part of a customer-requested migration -> no credit; consider goodwill one-time credit case-by-case.
- Evidence incomplete or inconclusive -> provisional small goodwill credit (e.g., up to $500) and plan deeper postmortem.

Examples of quick calculators (support guidance)
- If routed_region used instances with per-hour delta = $5/hr per node and 12 node-hours used -> delta = $60. Use this to frame small adjustments without Finance for < $250.

Customer comms best practices
- Be proactive and set clear timelines (initial ack within 4h, first update 72h).
- Use clear plain language — avoid internal jargon like 'pin enforcement'. Instead: 'requests were temporarily handled by our fallback region due to capacity constraints'.
- If offering credits, always attach the evidence pack summary and how the credit was calculated.

Open questions / Known risk flags (doc team follow-up)
- Consistent mapping between routing-reason-code and customer-facing explanation needs a glossary.
- Automated billing reconciliation when fallback uses Dedicated vs Hosted is still a gap (Finance owns).
- When fallback is partial (some sessions off-pin while others remain on-pin), create a per-session evidence extractor tool to speed calculations.

Quick links and resources
- How to export routing logs: confluence/region-routing/export-guide
- Billing CSV spec: finance/billing-export-spec-v2
- Engineering fallback reason codes: eng/ops/fallback-reasons.md

Last notes:
This is intended as a working support playbook — keep it lightweight. If a dispute escalates beyond $10k or triggers legal clauses, route to the CS Director + Legal immediately. We should iterate this doc after 3 real disputes to bake in common patterns and a shorter runbook for sub-$250 adjustments.

-- end of playbook --
